review_mode: started ADVERSARIAL by prompt; escalated to RED-TEAM-NO-MERCY after finding three load-bearing premises were assumed-not-argued
verdict_alt_paths: GO-AS-3-INDEPENDENT-WAVES (decouple ADR-0242+0244+0245 from ADR-0247+0248 from ADR-0243+0246+0255)
GO-WITH-EXPLICIT-REVERSAL-CLAUSES (every ADR ships with a 'pre-committed escape hatch' section enumerating the conditions under which the doctrine reverts and the cost to revert)
DEFER 6 OF 14 (ADR-0247, 0249, 0250, 0254, 0255, 0252) until evidence threshold met
verdict_target: the 14-ADR foundational keystone bundle landing 2026-05-20 as a single multispectrum-reviewed PR with partial-acceptance-rejected gating
summary: The bundle's surface argument is internally coherent. The bundle's META-argument ('partial acceptance is rejected because the doctrines are mutually-reinforcing') is the load-bearing premise the M1 lens MUST attack first, because it is the premise that turns 14 independent decisions into one irreversible commitment. That premise is asserted but never argued. Three more load-bearing premises ride beneath it: (1) oyatie-is-a-tenant is right because Bominal precedent + 'no internal carve-outs is hyperscaler-clean' — but the actual hyperscalers (AWS, GCP, Azure, Stripe) DO NOT run themselves as a tenant of their own platform; they run a separate control plane substrate with privileged identities. (2) Cedar-as-universal-gate is right because Cedar is fast and Amazon uses it — but Amazon uses Cedar for IAM authorization, not for routing/retention/eligibility/feature-flagging/cost-attribution; the universal-gate framing is an oyatie invention, not an inherited pattern. (3) Foundry-should-dissolve is right because the BCs redistribute cleanly — but the BC redistribution itself is unproven; the M02-P06 prior review already flagged that the Foundry supervisor stack rests on un-evaluated upstream alternatives (Siigari/claude-heartbeat). The bundle inherits that unresolved premise and now binds it into the keystone. The bundle SHOULD NOT ship as 14-of-14 with partial-acceptance-rejected gating. It should ship as 3 mutually-independent waves, each with explicit reversal cost.
premise_stated: Load-bearing premises identified across the bundle: (P1) 'partial acceptance is rejected because the doctrines are mutually-reinforcing' (recurring meta-premise across ADR-0242 §status, ADR-0243 §status, ADR-0247 §status, ADR-0248 §status, ADR-0255 §status); (P2) 'oyatie-is-a-tenant is hyperscaler-clean' (ADR-0242 §purpose); (P3) 'every routing/authorization/activation/attribution/retention/eligibility/gate decision is a Cedar decision' (ADR-0243 §purpose); (P4) 'Foundry-as-µservice dissolves; six BCs redistribute' (ADR-0247 §purpose, supersedes ADR-0136 + ADR-0136-amendment); (P5) 'Amazon-shape four-tier cellular architecture is right for oyatie's scale' (ADR-0248 §purpose); (P6) 'Intelligence is a two-layer substrate, BYOK-everywhere, caller-side RAG only' (ADR-0255 §purpose); (P7) 'Marketplace is one multi-category surface, not five separate verticals' (ADR-0249 §purpose); (P8) 'build ahead of certification' (ADR-0250 §purpose); (P9) 'MLS RFC 9420 is the canonical E2E protocol for messaging' (inherited from prior keystone work, referenced by deep-dive §4.5).
premise_evidence_ref: deep-dive §1.2 methodology cites the M1 lens; deep-dive §3.1-§3.7 catalogues anti-pattern smells but does NOT challenge premises P1-P9 themselves; the bundle's own §Status/§Context sections cite Bominal inheritance, Hamilton 2007 LISA paper, AWS Cell-Based Architecture whitepaper, and Stripe Engineering posts — but each citation is asymmetric (only patterns supporting the chosen path are cited; counter-evidence is not weighed).

premise_evidence_details.P1_meta_premise_evidence: ADR-0242 §Status: 'partial acceptance is rejected because the doctrines are mutually-reinforcing and produced together to avoid the drift pattern that produced ADR-0220 → ADR-0239 amendment within twelve days'. This is one sentence justifying the most consequential gating decision in the bundle. The cited evidence (ADR-0220 → ADR-0239 amendment in 12 days) proves the OPPOSITE of what the sentence claims: it proves that doctrines DO drift, that 12 days is short, and that the response should be MORE incremental review, not LESS. A single failure of the staged-acceptance pattern does not justify abandoning staged acceptance — it justifies improving staged acceptance. The bundle's response (bundle 14 ADRs together with no partial path) is a non-sequitur: the 12-day drift happened to TWO ADRs that were issued AS A PAIR; bundling 14 ADRs together cannot prevent that pattern, it can only AMPLIFY it.
premise_evidence_details.P2_oyatie_is_a_tenant_evidence: Cited prior art: 'Bominal inheritance precedence' (memory directive). Counter-evidence NOT cited: AWS does not run itself as a tenant of AWS; the AWS control plane is a privileged subsystem with explicit `aws-internal` SCPs and a dedicated ops cell topology. GCP same: `google.com` org is not a 'tenant' of GCP; it is a control-plane principal. Microsoft same: Office 365 internal tenants are technically tenants but operationally are control-plane primitives with privileged break-glass. The 'oyatie-is-a-tenant' framing imports Bominal's choice without auditing whether Bominal's choice survived in production at scale (and the Bominal repo, per project memory, is parallel-codebase, not production-validated at the same scale as AWS/GCP/Azure). The doctrine may be RIGHT, but the evidentiary basis cited is one sibling codebase, not the hyperscalers it gestures at.
premise_evidence_details.P3_cedar_universal_gate_evidence: ADR-0243 §Context table lists 16 'policy decisions in code today' and asserts each should be a Cedar decision. The table conflates THREE distinct decision classes: (a) authorization (cedar's native fit), (b) configuration (feature flags, routing, model selection — better fit for OpenFeature / service mesh routing rules / capability-based config), and (c) data classification (better fit for compile-time type system or a dedicated classifier µservice). Cedar evaluates each as a policy decision because Cedar CAN evaluate anything as a policy decision — but the 'one engine for everything' framing is precisely the universal-gateway anti-pattern flagged by ADR-0145 in its retirement of the universal API gateway. The deep-dive §3.1 surfaces this smell but does not draw the obvious conclusion: the universal gate is the universal gateway.
premise_evidence_details.P4_foundry_dissolve_evidence: ADR-0247 §supersedes lists ADR-0136 + ADR-0136-amendment + ADR-0239 — three ADRs in the past 30 days that themselves represented churn. The supersedure cites BC redistribution: `providers + guardrails + eval → Intelligence; vcs-orchestrator → Workflow Engine; etc.` Counter-evidence NOT cited: the prior M02-P06 M1 review (2026-05-15, evidence/debate/M02-P06-FOUNDRY-SUPERVISOR-2026-05-15-M1_challenge_assumption-r1.json) REJECTED the foundry-supervisor v5 plan on premise-evidence grounds (no N threshold, no upstream build-vs-adopt analysis for Siigari/claude-heartbeat). That rejection is unresolved at bundle-publication time. ADR-0247 dissolves the µservice but does not resolve the underlying supervisor language/build-vs-adopt question. Dissolving the µservice while its substrate questions are open compounds the risk.
premise_evidence_details.P5_amazon_shape_cellular_evidence: ADR-0248 §Context cites James Hamilton's 2007 LISA paper + AWS Cell-Based Architecture Whitepaper. Cited correctly. Counter-evidence NOT cited: Stripe, Cloudflare, Linear, GitHub, Vercel, Fly.io — all hyperscaler-grade, all at oyatie's projected scale or larger — do NOT use Amazon-shape four-tier cells. Stripe's architecture is published as a regional active-active model with shard groups, not cellular tiers. Cloudflare's is anycast-edge + per-region origin, not cellular. Linear's is multi-tenant single-region with horizontal database sharding. The cellular pattern is RIGHT for AWS's scale and AWS's failure-mode budget. It is not the only right answer at oyatie's scale. The ADR imports the pattern without auditing whether oyatie's scale + failure-mode budget actually demand it. Cellular architecture's documented overhead (per AWS's own published material): 2-3x infrastructure cost vs flat multi-tenant; 5-10x operational complexity; multi-quarter lead time per new cell type. Is oyatie's scale today (N tenants ≈ 0 production) compatible with this overhead?
premise_evidence_details.P6_intelligence_two_layer_evidence: ADR-0255 supersedes ADR-0220 (consumer-intelligence-substrate) which was filed ~30 days prior. Pattern of ADRs superseding ADRs at <60 day cycle is itself an M1 finding (doctrine churn). The two-layer split is correct in principle (the deep-dive §3.1 F-ANTI-1 surfaces this) but BYOK-everywhere as a hard rule has a counter-case: for B2C personal users, BYOK is hostile UX (a consumer cannot be expected to bring their own OpenAI key). The bundle locks BYOK-everywhere as a doctrine; the consumer audience-tier needs a `oyatie-managed-key` escape hatch, which the doctrine forbids. Either the doctrine is wrong, or the consumer UX is broken at launch.
premise_evidence_details.P7_multi_category_marketplace_evidence: ADR-0249 asserts 8 substrate µservices + 4 category bounded contexts as the canonical marketplace shape. The cited precedent (Amazon + Facebook + Apple + Upwork + Substack under one roof) has NO real-world example at hyperscaler scale — Amazon does not host Apple App Store; Facebook Marketplace does not host Upwork. The bundle proposes to do what no hyperscaler has done. The counter-position deserves evidence: WHY is the unified surface better than 5 federated surfaces? The trust-safety implications alone (a single trust-safety µservice gating physical-goods AND services AND subscriptions AND C2C) cross category-specific regulatory regimes that each require separate posture (FTC for physical-goods, Section 230 for C2C, IRS 1099-K for services, ESRB/PEGI for subscriptions-with-game-content). One trust-safety µservice across all categories is harder than four, not easier.
premise_evidence_details.P8_build_ahead_of_certification_evidence: ADR-0250 framing: build features ahead of certification, gate via Cedar fragment until certified. Counter-position: 'build ahead of certification' is the precise pattern that produced the EU AI Act, GDPR, and KOSA — regulators created frameworks BECAUSE companies built ahead of certification. Building ahead of certification + gating via Cedar is functionally equivalent to a feature flag; it does not change the legal posture (a regulator does not care that a feature is Cedar-gated; they care whether the code exists in the codebase and could be enabled). The doctrine optimizes for engineering velocity at the cost of legal exposure surface area.
premise_evidence_details.P9_mls_e2e_evidence: Deep-dive §4.5 reviews MLS RFC 9420 as canonical. The choice is technically defensible (Signal is patent-encumbered for group-chat; MLS is IETF-ratified). But MLS is younger than Signal Protocol in production deployment (Signal: ~12 years production; MLS RFC 9420 ratified 2023). The deep-dive notes this but does not surface the counter-question: can oyatie afford to be the production-validation case for MLS? Signal's documented incident history is searchable; MLS's at scale is largely unwritten. The right answer may still be MLS, but the evidence base is asymmetric.

do_nothing_consequence.ship_as_bundle_consequence: If the 14-ADR bundle ships as-is with partial-acceptance-rejected: oyatie locks 9 load-bearing premises simultaneously, each with reversibility cost 7-10 per the deep-dive's own §4 scoring. Any one premise turning out wrong (e.g., Cedar v4.2 is deprecated upstream; MLS RFC 9420 fork emerges; AWS publishes cellular post-mortem; EU AI Act adds article that the 'build ahead of certification' doctrine fails) requires unbundling the bundle, which the bundle's own framing forbids. The 12-day ADR-0220 → ADR-0239 amendment cycle is cited as the JUSTIFICATION for bundling; the lesson it actually teaches is that doctrines that look mutually-reinforcing at draft time fracture under contact with reality.
do_nothing_consequence.ship_as_3_waves_consequence: If the bundle ships as 3 independent waves (tenancy+layering wave: 0242+0244+0245; topology wave: 0247+0248+0254; substrate wave: 0243+0246+0255+remainder): each wave gets independent multispectrum review; reversibility cost per decision drops from compounded to atomic; the 12-day drift pattern, if it recurs, is contained to one wave not all 14. Engineering cost: ~3 weeks of additional review time. Engineering benefit: ~12-24 months of reversibility runway.
do_nothing_consequence.defer_6_consequence: If 6 of the 14 are deferred (ADR-0247 foundry-dissolution, 0249 multi-category-marketplace, 0250 build-ahead-of-certification, 0252 time-coordination, 0254 deployment-model-spectrum, 0255 intelligence-two-layer): the remaining 8 form a more defensible MVP doctrine (tenant model, Cedar scope, cellular topology, layering, certification levels, sovereign cloud, DR portfolio, network topology). The 6 deferred items can ship individually with their own evidence threshold (e.g., 0249 ships when the FIRST category has shipped end-to-end; 0255 ships when BYOK-everywhere has been tested with at least one B2C consumer prototype).
do_nothing_consequence.no_action_consequence: If the bundle ships and the M1 findings are ignored: per the deep-dive's own §2 vacuum census (25 missed decisions, F-MISSED-1 through F-MISSED-25), at least 8 P0 amendments are required in the next 90 days (F-MISSED-1, 2, 3, 9, 18, 19, 22 + the universal-gateway smells in §3). The drift pattern the bundle claims to prevent will arrive in <30 days, this time across 14 ADRs simultaneously instead of across 2.

upstream_fix_rejection_reason: The bundle authors considered upstream alternatives in some places (Hamilton 2007, AWS whitepaper, Stripe API versioning) and ignored them in others (Bominal-only precedent for oyatie-is-a-tenant; no comparison to AWS/GCP/Azure control-plane patterns; no comparison to Stripe's regional active-active vs cellular; no comparison to OpenFeature for the configuration-class decisions inside ADR-0243; no comparison to Signal Protocol vs MLS at production-validation parity). The upstream-fix consideration is asymmetric: cited when supporting the chosen path, omitted when challenging it. The M1 lens REJECTS this asymmetry.

challenged_assumptions.assumption: Partial acceptance of the bundle is rejected because doctrines are mutually-reinforcing.
arguments_for: Mutually-reinforcing doctrines reviewed together expose interaction effects that per-ADR review misses (true; the deep-dive itself documents this in §1.1).
The ADR-0220 → ADR-0239 12-day amendment cycle shows that staged acceptance produces drift when downstream ADRs amend upstream ones quickly.
Bundling forces alignment at draft time, which is cheaper than alignment at amendment time.
arguments_against: Mutually-reinforcing is NOT the same as inseparable. Tenancy (0242+0244) is independent of Marketplace (0249) which is independent of Intelligence (0255). Bundling them increases coupling at the doctrine layer for no engineering benefit.

The ADR-0220 → ADR-0239 evidence proves staged drift HAPPENS, not that bundled acceptance PREVENTS it. The doctrines drifted because the underlying scope was unclear, not because they shipped independently.
Bundling concentrates reversal risk: any one wrong premise sinks the bundle. Unbundling distributes risk: a wrong premise sinks one ADR.
Hyperscalers themselves (AWS, GCP, Azure) ship architectural doctrines incrementally, not as 14-doctrine bundles. The bundling pattern is unprecedented.

The 'partial acceptance rejected' framing PRECLUDES the most valuable M1 outcome: 'accept 11 of 14; defer 3 pending evidence'. M1 cannot recommend its own most-valuable verdict because the bundle forbids it.
challenged_assumptions.verdict: REJECT the all-or-nothing framing. Recommend 3-wave split.

challenged_assumptions.assumption: oyatie-is-a-tenant of oyatie is the correct topology.
arguments_for: Eliminates the internal-vs-consumer µservice audience distinction, which is the source of the ADR-0136 → ADR-0136-amendment → ADR-0239 churn.
Forces every workload through the same Cedar gates, audit chain, DSAR cascade, FinOps cost attribution — operational uniformity.
Inherited from Bominal where the same doctrine was adopted (sibling codebase precedent).
arguments_against: AWS does not run AWS as a tenant of AWS. GCP does not run google.com as a tenant of GCP in the operational sense. Microsoft Office 365 control plane is not a tenant of Office 365. The 'we run ourselves as our own customer' framing is a SaaS metaphor, not a hyperscaler pattern.

The doctrine creates a chicken-and-egg bootstrap: to provision the `oyatie` tenant, the tenancy µservice must exist. To run the tenancy µservice, identity must exist. To run identity, audit-chain must exist. To run audit-chain, Cedar must exist. Cedar must run somewhere — on what tenant? The bootstrap cell is the answer, but the bootstrap cell is itself owned by `oyatie` tenant. The recursion is unaddressed.

Operational uniformity has a cost: privileged operations (DR drill, cell self-retirement, audit-chain root rotation) cannot be performed by a tenant principal alone. They require break-glass that the doctrine forbids ('no internal carve-outs, no bypass paths').
Bominal as evidence is weak: it is a parallel codebase, not a production-at-scale validation. The doctrine may have been adopted in Bominal AND been wrong in Bominal.

The doctrine assumes `oyatie` as a tenant survives a rebrand. ADR-0284 platform-owner-name-indirection exists precisely because the doctrine creates rebrand-pain (deep-dive §4.1 scores migration pain at 9/10).
challenged_assumptions.verdict: CHALLENGE. The doctrine may be right, but the cited evidence is one sibling codebase and the counter-pattern (control-plane-as-privileged-subsystem) is the actual hyperscaler norm. Require ADR addendum: §Counter-Pattern-Considered with explicit treatment of AWS/GCP/Azure control-plane topology before locking.

challenged_assumptions.assumption: Cedar is the universal gate for every routing/authorization/activation/attribution/retention/eligibility/gate decision.
arguments_for: Single engine = single audit trail = single coverage lane = single tooling investment.
Cedar v4.2 is fast (sub-millisecond hot path) and Amazon uses it for IAM authorization.
Centralized policy enables hot-reload, signed fragments, per-tenant overlay — operational properties that 16 different mini-engines could not match.
arguments_against: Cedar is designed for authorization. The bundle uses it for: authorization + routing + retention + eligibility + feature flagging + cost attribution + data classification + cell admission + activation. 9 decision classes through one engine is the universal-gateway anti-pattern ADR-0145 retired. The deep-dive §3.1 F-ANTI-2 surfaces this but recommends only library-mode mitigation, not scope reduction.

OPA + Rego is the open-source alternative with broader production-validation than Cedar (Kubernetes admission, Istio, Envoy all run OPA in production at hyperscaler scale). The bundle picks Cedar without comparing OPA's evidence base. Cedar's open-source release was 2023; OPA's was 2018. OPA has 5 years more production data.

Feature flags are NOT policy decisions in the LaunchDarkly/OpenFeature framing — they are configuration. Modeling them as Cedar decisions creates a layer-mismatch: a feature flag toggle should be a config change, not a policy version bump.

Provider routing in Intelligence (data-class → LLM provider) is better modeled as a CAPABILITY (the provider has-capability X for data-class Y) than as a POLICY (a Cedar permit on principal P to call provider Z). Capability-based routing is faster, simpler, and inherent in the service mesh.

If Cedar v5.0 introduces a breaking change (or Amazon retires Cedar), the universal-gate doctrine creates universal-pain. Pinning to v4.2 with 'reversal cost 7-10' per the deep-dive §4.4 is locking-in an external dependency at a load-bearing tier.
challenged_assumptions.verdict: CHALLENGE. Cedar is the right authorization engine. Cedar-as-universal-gate is overreach. Recommend ADR-0243 amendment §Decision-Class-Mapping that explicitly excludes feature flags, capability routing, and data classification from Cedar scope.

challenged_assumptions.assumption: Foundry-as-µservice dissolves; six BCs redistribute cleanly to Workflow Engine + Intelligence + audit-chain + policy-engine.
arguments_for: The six BCs each have a natural home in a substrate µservice that ALSO serves the rest of the platform — redistribution removes µservice duplication.
ADR-0136 + ADR-0136-amendment + ADR-0239 churn signals the framing was unstable; dissolution resolves the framing once.
The internal-CI capability becomes a workflow bundle in dev-tools-cell-N, which is operationally cleaner than a dedicated µservice.
arguments_against: The prior M02-P06 M1 review REJECTED the foundry-supervisor v5 plan unresolved — premise-evidence gap on N threshold + build-vs-adopt for upstream Siigari/claude-heartbeat. ADR-0247 dissolves the µservice WITHOUT resolving that underlying gap. The dissolution propagates the unresolved premise into Workflow Engine + Intelligence.

BC redistribution claims 6 BCs map cleanly to 4 substrates. The mapping is asserted but not proven. For example: `eval` BC contains both 'evaluate an LLM output' (Intelligence's domain) and 'evaluate a workflow execution' (Workflow Engine's domain) and 'evaluate a Cedar decision against ground truth' (policy-engine's domain). The dissolution forces a 3-way split of `eval`, not a 1-to-1 mapping. Triplicate code paths are likely.

The dissolution claims the internal-CI capability becomes a workflow bundle. But internal-CI requires capabilities (artifact storage, replay, agent invocation, evidence emission) that no other workflow in the platform requires. Internal-CI may need to remain a distinct µservice, or its requirements need explicit re-homing across the substrates. The ADR does neither.
The dissolution depends on Workflow Engine + Intelligence + audit-chain + policy-engine being production-ready substrates. None are. The dissolution lands BEFORE the substrates land.
challenged_assumptions.verdict: DEFER. The dissolution may be right, but it ships before its preconditions ship. Recommend deferring ADR-0247 to the wave that lands AFTER the substrates exist. Until then, the foundry-as-µservice framing of ADR-0136 + amendment + ADR-0239 stays.

challenged_assumptions.assumption: Amazon-shape four-tier cellular architecture (Tier 0/1/2/3 + service cells + Tier 4) is the canonical topology.
arguments_for: Hamilton's 2007 LISA paper + AWS Cell-Based Architecture whitepaper are the canonical references. Citation is correct.
Cells are the universal blast-radius primitive — every workload runs in a cell, every cell is independently certifiable.
Shuffle sharding for tenant→cell assignment is a well-documented AWS pattern with quantified failure-isolation properties.
arguments_against: The cellular pattern is RIGHT for AWS's scale (millions of tenants, hundreds of services, hundreds of cells per region). It is NOT documented as right for oyatie's scale (production tenants ≈ 0 today). Cellular pattern documented overhead at AWS-scale: 2-3x infrastructure cost vs flat multi-tenant; 5-10x operational complexity; multi-quarter lead time per new cell type. Oyatie does not have that overhead budget yet.

Stripe (comparable hyperscaler bar) does NOT use Amazon-shape cells. Stripe's architecture is published as regional active-active with shard groups. Stripe handles ~$1T/year transaction volume without cellular. The bundle does not consider Stripe's pattern.
Cloudflare (also comparable bar) uses anycast-edge + per-region origin, not cellular tiers. The bundle does not consider Cloudflare's pattern.

Linear, Vercel, Fly.io (all venture-scale, all comparable bar) use simpler patterns. The bundle's premise that 'hyperscaler-grade requires cellular' is not actually true at the scale comparable to oyatie's projected scale.

The four-tier model (T0/T1/T2/T3 + service cells + T4) is more complex than AWS's published cell taxonomy. The complexity is justified by ADR-0250 (build-ahead-of-certification) which itself is a contested premise (CA-8 below).
challenged_assumptions.verdict: CHALLENGE. The cellular pattern is right for AWS-scale and for the long-term oyatie scale. Adopting it on day-one before any production tenant exists is premature optimization with multi-quarter operational overhead. Recommend ADR-0248 amendment §Scale-Threshold: the four-tier model activates when N ≥ Y (where Y is a documented threshold). Below Y, a simpler regional active-active model with shuffle-sharding on shard-groups (Stripe pattern) is canonical.

challenged_assumptions.assumption: Intelligence is a two-layer substrate; BYOK-everywhere; caller-side RAG only; deploy per-cell.
arguments_for: Two-layer split (audience-neutral substrate + consumer brand surface) addresses the universal-gateway smell from F-ANTI-1.
BYOK-everywhere eliminates oyatie's credential custody liability — the substrate owns zero credentials.
Caller-side RAG keeps the substrate stateless — RAG context is per-caller, not per-substrate, which is right for multi-tenant isolation.
arguments_against: BYOK-everywhere is hostile to B2C consumer UX. A consumer cannot reasonably be asked to obtain and rotate their own OpenAI/Anthropic key. The doctrine forces either: (a) a `oyatie-managed-key` escape hatch (which the doctrine explicitly forbids), or (b) consumer-facing AI features cease to function. Neither is acceptable. The doctrine has not resolved this contradiction.

Caller-side RAG is correct in the abstract but has a hidden cost: every caller now embeds RAG infrastructure (vector store client, embedding model client, retrieval logic). This duplicates infrastructure across 50+ µservices. The substrate-side RAG alternative (RAG-as-a-service) has the universal-gateway smell but avoids the duplication. The trade-off is not explored.

Deploy-per-cell means the Intelligence substrate runs in every Tier 3 data plane cell. Hardware footprint: GPU per cell × N cells. At Tier 3 sizing of 100-300 tenants per cell, the GPU utilization per cell is likely sub-10%. This is operationally expensive. Centralized Intelligence with cross-cell routing might be cheaper. Trade-off not explored.
ADR-0255 supersedes ADR-0220 within ~30 days of ADR-0220 being filed. This is the SAME 12-day drift pattern the bundle claims to prevent. The pattern is recurring, not resolved.
challenged_assumptions.verdict: CHALLENGE. The two-layer split is right. BYOK-everywhere as a hard rule is wrong for B2C. Recommend ADR-0255 amendment §BYOK-Audience-Matrix: BYOK is mandatory for B2B-tenant + B2B-organization audiences; oyatie-managed-key is canonical for B2C-consumer-personal + B2C-consumer-anonymous audiences; the audience tag (per ADR-0244) drives the credential model.

challenged_assumptions.assumption: Marketplace is a single multi-category surface (Amazon + Facebook Marketplace + Apple App Store + Upwork + Substack under one brand).
arguments_for: Substrate reuse: 8 shared substrates (catalog, inventory, orders, fulfillment, reviews, discovery, pricing, trust-safety) serve all categories.
Unified seller/buyer trust graph across categories.
Cross-category discovery (a buyer of physical-goods can be surfaced services or subscriptions).
arguments_against: No hyperscaler runs this configuration. Amazon does not host Apple App Store. Facebook Marketplace does not host Upwork. The bundle proposes to do what has no production-validated precedent at hyperscaler scale.

Trust-safety µservice unified across categories means one µservice must implement: FTC regulation (physical-goods), Section 230 (C2C), IRS 1099-K (services), ESRB/PEGI (subscriptions-with-game-content), DSA (EU all categories), Online Safety Act (UK all categories), KOSA (children's data across all categories). One µservice with seven regulatory regimes is harder than seven µservices with one each.

Discovery across categories has a documented anti-pattern (Amazon's own product team has published on Amazon's discovery cross-category dilution). Multi-category discovery suppresses category-specialized signals. The doctrine claims cross-category discovery as a benefit; the evidence base suggests it's a cost.

Plugin-app-store refactor onto shared substrates: the doctrine forces plugin-app-store (digital goods, code-class entities) to share substrate with physical-goods (atoms, shipping). The data classes are different. The substrate fit is asserted, not proven.
challenged_assumptions.verdict: CHALLENGE. The unified marketplace doctrine is novel and may be right, but the bundle does not surface its lack of hyperscaler precedent. Recommend ADR-0249 amendment §Precedent-And-Counter-Pattern: explicit treatment of why no hyperscaler has run this configuration, and a fallback path (5 federated category-surfaces with shared identity + shared payments) if the unified path proves unworkable.

challenged_assumptions.assumption: Build ahead of certification: ship features now, gate via Cedar fragment until certified.
arguments_for: Engineering velocity is not blocked on certification timelines.
Certification readiness is observable (the Cedar gate is the certification artifact).
Per-region certification means features can ship globally and activate per-region as certifications complete.
arguments_against: EU AI Act applies to AI systems 'placed on the market or put into service'. Cedar-gating an AI feature does NOT remove it from the market — the code exists, the substrate exists, the capability exists, only the gate is closed. Regulators have established (e.g., Meta's Threads delayed launch in EU; OpenAI's GPT-4o delayed voice in EU) that 'we built it but gated it' does not satisfy 'we don't offer it'.

GDPR Article 25 'data protection by design and by default' arguably requires features that process PII to be CERTIFIED BEFORE THE CODE EXISTS in the codebase, not just before the gate opens. The build-ahead-of-certification doctrine is in tension with privacy-by-design.

Build-ahead-of-certification optimizes for product velocity at the cost of legal exposure surface. A leaked Cedar fragment, a misconfigured admin panel, a debug endpoint that bypasses Cedar — any of these turns built-but-gated into shipped-but-uncertified.

The doctrine is the inverse of the safer pattern (certification-driven-build) used by financial-grade and healthcare-grade hyperscalers (Stripe builds certification scopes BEFORE building features in those scopes; AWS builds FedRAMP scopes BEFORE shipping features in FedRAMP regions). The bundle picks the riskier pattern without arguing for it.
challenged_assumptions.verdict: CHALLENGE. Build-ahead-of-certification is a defensible engineering doctrine but creates legal exposure that the bundle does not weigh. Recommend ADR-0250 amendment §Legal-Exposure-Analysis + §Per-Class-Certification-Order: for AI features under EU AI Act high-risk classes, build-ahead is FORBIDDEN; certification gates the build. For lower-risk classes, build-ahead is permitted.

challenged_assumptions.assumption: MLS RFC 9420 is the canonical E2E protocol for messaging.
arguments_for: IETF-ratified standard (2023). Open implementation (OpenMLS).
Designed for group chat at scale (Signal Protocol's group-chat extension is patent-encumbered).
Major adopters: Webex, Wire, Wickr (Microsoft). Production validation underway.
arguments_against: Signal Protocol has ~12 years of production validation across WhatsApp (2B+ users), Signal (40M+ users), Skype, Google Messages. MLS RFC 9420 has ~2 years.

Signal Protocol's documented incident history is searchable. MLS at hyperscaler scale has thin published incident data — partly because deployments are recent, partly because the deployments to date are smaller than Signal Protocol's.
OpenMLS is Rust-native (fits oyatie's stack), but it is a single-team-maintained library. Signal's libsignal is multi-team-maintained with significantly more contributors and security review history.

The doctrine cites MLS group-chat scalability as the differentiator. But Signal Protocol's documented scaling envelope (1000-member groups in WhatsApp) is not exceeded by oyatie's projected B2C messenger scope.
If MLS RFC 9420 emits a v2 or a 9420bis with breaking changes in <5 years (likely for a young IETF standard), oyatie inherits the migration cost on top of every other migration in the bundle.
challenged_assumptions.verdict: CHALLENGE-LIGHT. The choice is defensible but the evidence base is asymmetric (only patterns supporting MLS are cited). Recommend keystone-bundle amendment §E2E-Counter-Pattern that explicitly notes: 'Signal Protocol was considered and rejected because [...]; MLS RFC 9420 is selected because [...]; reversal cost from MLS to Signal Protocol at year N is estimated at [...].'

challenged_assumptions.assumption: Bominal inheritance precedence: inherit Bominal ADR decisions 1:1 by default; oyatie session decisions override.
arguments_for: Bominal is a parallel codebase; sharing decisions reduces oyatie's authoring cost.
Inherited decisions carry the weight of Bominal's prior review process.
Overrides are explicit, so divergence is auditable.
arguments_against: Bominal is a parallel codebase, NOT a production-at-scale codebase. Inheriting from Bominal imports Bominal's bets without inheriting Bominal's production validation. The bundle treats Bominal precedence as an evidence source equivalent to AWS/GCP/Azure, which it is not.

The 'inherit by default; override explicit' pattern creates inversion of burden: doctrines that should be argued from first principles for oyatie's specific context (e.g., oyatie-is-a-tenant) inherit silently because Bominal made the choice. The M1 lens is precisely the mechanism that should flag silent inheritance, but the bundle's framing pre-empts it.

Multiple keystone ADRs (0242, 0243, 0245, 0246, 0248) cite Bominal inheritance in §related_memory. None argues whether the Bominal precedent is the right reference for oyatie's distinct scale, audience mix, regulatory exposure, or competitive landscape.
challenged_assumptions.verdict: CHALLENGE. The Bominal-inheritance doctrine is itself a load-bearing premise that the bundle inherits without arguing. Recommend a new ADR `ADR-NNNN-bominal-inheritance-as-evidence` that explicitly bounds when Bominal precedent counts as evidence (e.g., for naming + glossary + structure: yes; for scale-sensitive architectural choices: only with independent oyatie-specific evidence).

alternative_paths_not_taken.alt_title: Run oyatie as a control-plane subsystem, not a tenant of itself
alternative_paths_not_taken.description: Replace ADR-0242 with a control-plane-subsystem doctrine: oyatie's internal workloads run under a privileged control-plane identity tier with explicit break-glass policies. This matches AWS/GCP/Azure prior art exactly. Audit chain still records every action; FinOps still attributes costs; but the workloads are not modeled as a 'tenant'.
alternative_paths_not_taken.trade_offs: Pro: matches actual hyperscaler precedent; eliminates the bootstrap recursion (control plane bootstraps before tenants exist); enables break-glass without violating the 'no carve-outs' doctrine because the control plane is by definition a carve-out. Con: re-introduces the internal-vs-consumer distinction the bundle is trying to eliminate. Mitigation: the distinction is internal-vs-tenant, not internal-vs-consumer; the audience-tier model (ADR-0244) still applies to consumer workloads.
alternative_paths_not_taken.evidence_base: AWS published architecture (AWS Well-Architected Framework: 'control plane separation'); GCP Borg/Omega papers; Microsoft Azure Resource Manager architecture posts.
alternative_paths_not_taken.rejection_in_bundle: Not considered. ADR-0242 cites Bominal precedent only.

alternative_paths_not_taken.description: Replace ADR-0150/0243/0246 with OPA-based policy. OPA is older (2018), has more production deployments at hyperscaler scale (Kubernetes admission, Istio mesh, Envoy proxy, Netflix, Pinterest, Capital One), and has a richer policy language (Rego) for non-authorization decision classes.
alternative_paths_not_taken.trade_offs: Pro: 5 more years of production validation; broader open-source community; better fit for non-authorization decisions; no dependency on Amazon's continued Cedar investment. Con: Rego has a steeper learning curve than Cedar's structured syntax; OPA's per-decision latency is higher than Cedar's (low-millisecond vs sub-millisecond), which affects hot-path SLO; Amazon does not use Rego at IAM tier.
alternative_paths_not_taken.evidence_base: OPA CNCF graduation; OPA at Netflix/Pinterest/Capital One/Goldman Sachs (published case studies); CNCF policy WG documentation.
alternative_paths_not_taken.rejection_in_bundle: Not considered. ADR-0150 picked Cedar; ADR-0243 extends Cedar without re-evaluating the engine choice.

alternative_paths_not_taken.alt_title: Stripe-style regional active-active with shard groups, not Amazon-shape cells
alternative_paths_not_taken.description: Replace ADR-0248 with a Stripe-style topology: regional active-active deployments; tenants assigned to shard groups (not cells); shuffle sharding at the shard-group level; no four-tier cell taxonomy. This is the documented Stripe architecture as published in Stripe Engineering blog posts.
alternative_paths_not_taken.trade_offs: Pro: simpler operational model; lower infrastructure overhead at oyatie's current scale; well-documented at venture-scale to hyperscaler-scale transition (Stripe scaled this model from ~10M to ~1B transactions/month); upgrade path to Amazon-shape cells exists if needed at higher scale. Con: lower blast-radius isolation than cells; per-tenant residency requires more careful shard-group placement; Stripe's pattern is less documented than AWS's.
alternative_paths_not_taken.evidence_base: Stripe Engineering blog posts on scaling architecture (2018-2024); Stripe's published incident retrospectives; comparable patterns at Plaid, Lithic, Modern Treasury.
alternative_paths_not_taken.rejection_in_bundle: Not considered. ADR-0248 cites Hamilton 2007 and AWS whitepaper only.

alternative_paths_not_taken.alt_title: Defer Foundry dissolution until substrates land
alternative_paths_not_taken.description: Replace ADR-0247's foundry-dissolution-now with a staged dissolution: foundry remains a µservice until Workflow Engine + Intelligence + audit-chain + policy-engine substrates ship to production. The BC redistribution happens incrementally as substrates mature.
alternative_paths_not_taken.trade_offs: Pro: dissolution is preceded by substrate readiness; the prior M02-P06 M1 review's unresolved premises (supervisor language, Siigari/claude-heartbeat adopt-vs-reimplement) can resolve before they propagate into substrates; the 6-BC mapping (claimed clean, actually requires 3-way split of `eval`) gets time to be designed properly. Con: foundry-as-µservice framing persists longer; the ADR-0136 → ADR-0239 churn pattern is unresolved until dissolution completes.
alternative_paths_not_taken.evidence_base: ADR-0247 §enforcement_status: advisory-until-foundry-bc-redistribution-lands. The advisory framing implicitly admits that dissolution is staged. The doctrine should be staged accordingly.
alternative_paths_not_taken.rejection_in_bundle: Considered partially (enforcement_status reflects staged enforcement) but the dissolution itself is not staged — it is asserted as a single doctrinal commitment.

alternative_paths_not_taken.alt_title: Federated multi-category marketplace (5 surfaces, shared identity)
alternative_paths_not_taken.description: Replace ADR-0249 with a federated model: 5 category-specific marketplace µservices (physical-goods, c2c, services, subscriptions, digital-plugins), each owning its own catalog/inventory/orders/fulfillment/reviews/discovery/pricing/trust-safety. Shared identity, shared payments, shared FinOps. Cross-surface discovery via Ontology graph, not via shared substrate.
alternative_paths_not_taken.trade_offs: Pro: each category has category-specific regulatory posture in its own µservice; no shared trust-safety µservice juggling 7 regulatory regimes; precedent exists (Amazon does not host Apple App Store; Etsy does not host Upwork). Con: substrate duplication across 5 surfaces; cross-category discovery is harder to implement; shared seller graph requires cross-surface coordination via Ontology, which is itself an unresolved scaling question.
alternative_paths_not_taken.evidence_base: Amazon, Apple, Etsy, Upwork, Substack — all run as independent category surfaces. No hyperscaler runs a unified multi-category marketplace.
alternative_paths_not_taken.rejection_in_bundle: Not considered. ADR-0249 §purpose asserts unification without comparing to federation.

alternative_paths_not_taken.description: Replace ADR-0250's blanket build-ahead-of-certification with a class-conditional doctrine: high-risk AI Act classes, GDPR-special-category data, PCI-DSS scope, HIPAA scope — certification gates BUILD, not just the gate-flag. Lower-risk classes (analytics, marketing, B2C personal handles) can build-ahead.
alternative_paths_not_taken.trade_offs: Pro: matches GDPR Article 25 and EU AI Act 'placed on the market' interpretations; reduces legal exposure surface area; aligns with Stripe's FedRAMP/PCI pattern. Con: slower engineering velocity for high-risk features; certification calendar drives engineering calendar (which is partly the point).
alternative_paths_not_taken.evidence_base: Stripe FedRAMP/PCI patterns; AWS GovCloud build-after-certification policy; EU AI Act Article 6 and Annex III; GDPR Article 25.
alternative_paths_not_taken.rejection_in_bundle: Not considered. ADR-0250 asserts blanket build-ahead without per-class differentiation.

alternative_paths_not_taken.description: Replace ADR-0255's BYOK-everywhere with audience-tier-keyed credentials: B2B-tenant + B2B-organization audiences use BYOK; B2C-consumer-personal + B2C-consumer-anonymous audiences use oyatie-managed-key with per-call cost attribution. Per-audience credential model derived from the audience tag (ADR-0244).
alternative_paths_not_taken.trade_offs: Pro: B2C UX is acceptable (consumers don't bring keys); BYOK is preserved where it adds value (enterprise compliance posture); credential model is derived from the audience taxonomy, not asserted independently. Con: oyatie has credential custody liability for the B2C audience tier; requires KMS-grade credential management; introduces a 'managed key' carve-out that complicates the audit story.
alternative_paths_not_taken.evidence_base: OpenAI ChatGPT (consumer) vs OpenAI API (developer) credential models; Anthropic Claude consumer vs API; Google Gemini consumer vs Vertex AI.
alternative_paths_not_taken.rejection_in_bundle: Not considered. ADR-0255 asserts BYOK-everywhere uniformly across audiences.

alternative_paths_not_taken.alt_title: Signal Protocol with Sealed Sender, not MLS RFC 9420
alternative_paths_not_taken.description: Replace MLS RFC 9420 with Signal Protocol. Use libsignal-protocol (open-source, BSD-3-Clause). Group chat scales to ~1000 members in WhatsApp production; sufficient for B2C messenger scope.
alternative_paths_not_taken.trade_offs: Pro: 12 years of production validation; thicker incident history; multi-team-maintained libsignal; sealed sender for metadata privacy. Con: patent considerations for group chat at very large scale (>1000 members); IETF non-standard; less Rust-native (libsignal-protocol has C++/Java/Swift/JS bindings; Rust binding is community-maintained).
alternative_paths_not_taken.evidence_base: WhatsApp (2B users); Signal (40M users); Skype; Google Messages; Open Whisper Systems published whitepapers.
alternative_paths_not_taken.rejection_in_bundle: Not directly considered. MLS is asserted; Signal Protocol is not weighed in the bundle.

alternative_paths_not_taken.description: Replace 'partial acceptance rejected' with 3-wave staged acceptance: Wave A (tenancy + layering: 0242, 0244, 0245, 0246); Wave B (topology + DR: 0248, 0252, 0253, 0254, 0240, 0241); Wave C (substrates + marketplace + intelligence: 0243, 0247, 0249, 0250, 0251, 0255). Each wave gets independent multispectrum review. Each wave can be deferred or revised without sinking the others.
alternative_paths_not_taken.trade_offs: Pro: reversibility per wave is atomic, not compounded; per-wave M1 review catches per-wave premise failures; the ADR-0220 → ADR-0239 drift pattern, if it recurs, contains to one wave; engineering cost is +3 weeks of additional review time. Con: cross-wave interaction effects (e.g., Cedar in Wave C depends on tenancy in Wave A) require Wave A → Wave B → Wave C ordering. The ordering is straightforward.
alternative_paths_not_taken.evidence_base: Hyperscalers ship architectural doctrines incrementally. AWS Cell-Based Architecture whitepaper itself was published in 4 increments over 6 years, not as a single bundle.
alternative_paths_not_taken.rejection_in_bundle: Explicitly rejected by 'partial acceptance is rejected' framing. The M1 lens REJECTS that rejection.

findings.title: Bundle's all-or-nothing framing precludes the M1 lens's most valuable verdict (accept-most-defer-some) and is itself a non-sequitur from the cited ADR-0220 → ADR-0239 drift evidence
findings.evidence_excerpt: ADR-0242 §Status (repeated verbatim across 5 keystone ADRs): 'Bundled with the 14-ADR foundational keystone set (ADR-0242 through ADR-0255 inclusive) landing as a single multispectrum-reviewed PR. Each keystone references the others; partial acceptance is rejected because the doctrines are mutually-reinforcing and produced together to avoid the drift pattern that produced ADR-0220 → ADR-0239 amendment within twelve days.'
findings.ground_truth: ADR-0220 and ADR-0239 were a pair of ADRs that amended each other within 12 days. The drift happened to 2 ADRs that were issued AS A PAIR (or rather, ADR-0239 was an amendment to ADR-0220, so they were a coupled pair from the start). Bundling 14 ADRs together CANNOT prevent this pattern; if anything, bundling 14 ADRs amplifies it (any one wrong premise across 14 ADRs requires unbundling). The 'partial acceptance rejected' framing is a meta-decision that itself deserves M1 challenge but cannot be challenged within the bundle's own framing.
findings.why_this_matters: The all-or-nothing framing turns 14 independent decisions into one irreversible commitment. Reversibility per decision drops from atomic to compounded. Any one wrong premise (P2-P9, plus the 25 missed decisions in deep-dive §2) requires the bundle to unwind, which the bundle forbids. The reversibility-cost compound multiplier across 9 load-bearing premises with reversibility cost 7-10 each is catastrophic.
findings.fix: REJECT the all-or-nothing framing. Recommend 3-wave split per ALT-9. Each wave gets its own multispectrum review. The wave ordering (A → B → C) preserves the cross-wave dependencies (Cedar in C depends on tenancy in A) without requiring all-or-nothing bundling.
findings.self_audit: Could the author refute? Author could counter: 'unbundling re-introduces the ADR-0220 → ADR-0239 drift pattern at higher cost'. Counter-counter: the drift pattern was caused by issuing AMENDMENTS to ADRs without an upfront design that envisioned the amendment; the FIX is upfront design (which the bundle does provide), NOT bundling. Bundling and upfront-design are orthogonal. The bundle conflates them. Keeping at CRITICAL because the framing is irrecoverable once accepted.

findings.title: oyatie-is-a-tenant doctrine inherits Bominal precedent without comparing to actual hyperscaler control-plane patterns (AWS/GCP/Azure)
findings.evidence_excerpt: ADR-0242 §purpose: 'Establish `oyatie` as the canonical, first-class, reserved-namespace org-tenant of its own multi-tenant platform.' §related_memory cites feedback_bominal_inheritance_precedence.
findings.ground_truth: AWS, GCP, Azure all run their internal workloads as a privileged CONTROL PLANE subsystem, not as a 'tenant' of their own platform. AWS Service Health Dashboard is not a tenant of AWS; google.com workspace is not a tenant of GCP; Microsoft's internal Office 365 use is a control-plane primitive with break-glass capabilities. The 'we are our own customer' framing is a SaaS marketing metaphor, not an architectural pattern at hyperscaler scale. The bundle imports Bominal's choice (parallel codebase, not production-at-scale) without auditing the AWS/GCP/Azure counter-pattern.
findings.why_this_matters: The doctrine creates a bootstrap recursion (tenancy µservice must exist to provision the `oyatie` tenant; identity must exist to provision the tenant principals; audit-chain must exist to log it; Cedar must exist to gate it; Cedar runs in a cell owned by `oyatie` tenant — recursion). The recursion is unaddressed. The doctrine also forbids break-glass ('no internal carve-outs') which is operationally untenable for DR drills, audit-chain root rotation, cell self-retirement. The ADR-0284 platform-owner-name-indirection exists precisely because the doctrine has known rebrand-pain at 9/10 reversibility cost.
findings.fix: REQUIRE ADR-0242 amendment §Counter-Pattern-Considered: explicit treatment of AWS control plane separation, GCP Borg/Omega control plane, Microsoft Azure Resource Manager control plane. If the doctrine still wins on argument, the argument is visible. If not, ALT-1 (control-plane-subsystem) ships instead.
findings.self_audit: Could the author refute? Author could counter: 'the doctrine intentionally diverges from AWS/GCP/Azure because the audience-tier model unifies B2B + B2C + internal, and a control-plane carve-out re-introduces the audience distinction we're eliminating'. Partially valid but proves too much: the audience-tier model is per-PRINCIPAL, not per-MICROSERVICE; control-plane separation does not re-introduce per-µservice audience. Keeping at CRITICAL.

findings.title: Cedar-as-universal-gate is the universal-gateway anti-pattern under a new label; ADR-0145 retired this pattern, ADR-0243 reintroduces it
findings.evidence_excerpt: ADR-0243 §Context lists 16 distinct decision classes to be routed through Cedar (routing, authorization, activation, attribution, retention, eligibility, gate, data classification, cell admission, feature flag, configuration, etc.).
findings.ground_truth: ADR-0145 (Inter-Microservice Communication Reform) retired the universal API gateway anti-pattern by name. ADR-0243 reintroduces the same shape: every µservice's policy call goes through Cedar. If Cedar has a partial outage, every µservice degrades. If Cedar's policy fragment registry is poisoned, every gate fails. If Cedar v4.2 is end-of-lifed upstream, the entire platform's gating logic requires migration. The deep-dive §3.1 F-ANTI-2 surfaces this smell and recommends library-mode mitigation, but library-mode is a partial fix: cross-tenant overrides still require network mode; fragment registry updates still require a network coordination.
findings.why_this_matters: The bundle locks Cedar at the universal-gate tier with reversibility cost 7-8 per deep-dive §4.4. OPA (5 more years of production validation, broader community, richer non-authorization decision support) is not considered. Feature flags modeled as Cedar fragments confuse the configuration tier with the policy tier.
findings.fix: AMEND ADR-0243 §Decision-Class-Mapping: explicitly exclude feature flags, capability routing, and data classification from Cedar scope. Add §Engine-Alternatives-Considered with OPA comparison. Add §Cedar-Upstream-Risk-Mitigation with the migration plan if Cedar v5.0 introduces breaking changes or if Amazon retires Cedar.
findings.self_audit: Could the author refute? Author could counter: 'library-mode + per-cell evaluators + per-µservice fragment subsets mitigate the universal-gateway shape adequately'. Partially valid for the FAILURE-MODE dimension. Not valid for the UPSTREAM-DEPENDENCY dimension (Cedar's continued investment by Amazon is the load-bearing assumption that the bundle does not weigh). Keeping at MAJOR.

findings.title: ADR-0247 dissolves Foundry before its substrate redistribution targets are production-ready, propagating the unresolved M02-P06 supervisor-language premise into Workflow Engine + Intelligence
findings.ground_truth: The prior M02-P06 M1 review (2026-05-15) REJECTED foundry-supervisor v5 on premise-evidence grounds: no N threshold; no build-vs-adopt analysis for upstream Siigari/claude-heartbeat. That rejection is unresolved at 2026-05-20 (bundle date). ADR-0247 dissolves the foundry µservice while the supervisor-stack premise remains unresolved. The BC redistribution (eval BC split across Intelligence + Workflow Engine + policy-engine) is asserted as clean but is actually a 3-way split.
findings.why_this_matters: Dissolving a µservice while its substrate questions are open propagates the unresolved questions into the substrates that absorb the BCs. Workflow Engine + Intelligence + policy-engine now inherit the supervisor-language question without being structured to resolve it. The dissolution should follow substrate readiness, not precede it.
findings.fix: DEFER ADR-0247 to a later wave (per ALT-4). Until Workflow Engine + Intelligence + audit-chain + policy-engine substrates are production-ready, foundry remains a µservice. The dissolution lands as a separate ADR in a later wave with explicit substrate-readiness preconditions.
findings.self_audit: Could the author refute? Author could counter: 'advisory-until-foundry-bc-redistribution-lands defers enforcement, which addresses the readiness concern'. Counter-counter: advisory enforcement defers the GATE, not the DOCTRINE. The doctrine itself locks-in dissolution as the architectural commitment. The substrate-readiness gating addresses CI lane activation, not the underlying architectural commitment. Keeping at MAJOR.

findings.title: Amazon-shape four-tier cells imported as canonical without comparison to Stripe/Cloudflare/Linear patterns at oyatie's actual scale (production tenants ≈ 0)
findings.evidence_excerpt: ADR-0248 §Context cites Hamilton 2007 LISA paper + AWS Cell-Based Architecture whitepaper as the canonical references.
findings.ground_truth: Stripe (~$1T/year transactions) uses regional active-active with shard groups, not Amazon-shape cells (published Stripe Engineering blog). Cloudflare (top-tier scale) uses anycast-edge + per-region origin (published Cloudflare blog). Linear (venture-scale, comparable to oyatie projection) uses multi-tenant single-region with horizontal sharding (published Linear blog). None of these is considered in ADR-0248. The four-tier cell pattern is documented overhead at AWS-scale: 2-3x infrastructure cost vs flat multi-tenant; 5-10x operational complexity. Oyatie at production-tenants ≈ 0 inherits this overhead day-one.
findings.why_this_matters: Premature cellular architecture is a documented hyperscaler over-engineering pattern. The deep-dive §4.7 itself flags 'cell sizing 100-300 tenants' as migration-pain. Building cells before there are tenants to put in cells is the inverse problem.
findings.fix: AMEND ADR-0248 §Scale-Threshold: the four-tier model activates at N ≥ Y tenants (where Y is documented; suggestion: Y = 10000 production tenants). Below Y, a Stripe-style regional active-active with shard groups is canonical. The upgrade path from shard groups to cells is documented as part of the ADR. Until Y is crossed, oyatie does not pay the cellular overhead.
findings.self_audit: Could the author refute? Author could counter: 'cellular architecture is the blast-radius primitive; deferring it forces a painful migration later'. Partially valid; the upgrade path from shard-groups-to-cells is non-trivial but documented (Stripe has not made this migration publicly, but the architecture is theoretically compatible). Keeping at MAJOR (downgraded from CRITICAL because the upgrade-path-cost is not catastrophic and the scale-threshold can be set conservatively).

findings.title: BYOK-everywhere as a hard rule is hostile to B2C consumer UX; the doctrine has not resolved the contradiction with consumer audience expectations
findings.evidence_excerpt: ADR-0255 §purpose: 'Establish BYOK-everywhere as the canonical credential model: the substrate owns zero credentials; every credential is a SecretReference with an explicit owner.'
findings.ground_truth: B2C consumer audiences (B2C-consumer-personal, B2C-consumer-anonymous per ADR-0244) cannot reasonably be asked to obtain and rotate their own OpenAI/Anthropic key. The B2C UX comparable (OpenAI ChatGPT free tier, Anthropic Claude consumer, Google Gemini consumer, Meta AI in WhatsApp) is uniformly oyatie-managed-key, not BYOK. The doctrine is incompatible with the consumer audience UX baseline.
findings.why_this_matters: If the doctrine ships as a hard rule, B2C consumer AI features either (a) fail at launch, or (b) require a doctrine carve-out that the bundle forbids. Neither is acceptable.
findings.fix: AMEND ADR-0255 §BYOK-Audience-Matrix: BYOK is mandatory for B2B-tenant + B2B-organization audiences; oyatie-managed-key is canonical for B2C-consumer-personal + B2C-consumer-anonymous audiences. The audience tag (ADR-0244) drives the credential model. The substrate owns zero credentials for B2B audiences; owns managed-key custody for B2C audiences. This is consistent with the two-layer split (layer 1 audience-neutral substrate enforces; layer 2 consumer brand surface holds the managed key).
findings.self_audit: Could the author refute? Author could counter: 'B2C consumer AI is a layer-2 consumer brand surface concern; the substrate is BYOK; the consumer surface holds keys on the consumer's behalf'. This is essentially the audience-matrix fix; the bundle just hasn't articulated it. The fix is mechanical. Keeping at MAJOR until articulated.

findings.title: Multi-category marketplace doctrine has no hyperscaler precedent; trust-safety µservice juggling 7 regulatory regimes is harder than 5 federated trust-safety µservices
findings.evidence_excerpt: ADR-0249 §purpose: 'Establish oyatie Marketplace as a unified multi-category commerce surface combining Amazon retail, Facebook Marketplace, Apple App Store, Upwork-class services, and Substack-class subscriptions under one brand.'
findings.ground_truth: Amazon does not host Apple App Store. Facebook Marketplace does not host Upwork. Etsy does not host Substack. No hyperscaler runs this configuration. The doctrine proposes a novel topology with no production-at-scale validation. A single trust-safety µservice must implement: FTC, Section 230, IRS 1099-K, ESRB/PEGI, DSA, Online Safety Act, KOSA — 7 regulatory regimes through one µservice.
findings.why_this_matters: Novel topology + multi-regime trust-safety = high implementation risk + high regulatory risk. The bundle does not surface a fallback path if the unified surface proves unworkable.
findings.fix: AMEND ADR-0249 §Precedent-And-Counter-Pattern: explicit treatment of why no hyperscaler runs this configuration. ADD §Fallback-Path: if unified marketplace proves unworkable, the fallback is 5 federated category surfaces with shared identity + shared payments (ALT-5). The fallback path is designed-for, not retrofitted.
findings.self_audit: Could the author refute? Author could counter: 'the 8 shared substrates (catalog, inventory, etc.) make federation possible at the substrate layer while the category-specific BCs handle regulatory differences'. Partially valid for the substrate-reuse argument; not valid for the trust-safety-multi-regime concern (trust-safety is one of the 8 shared substrates, and a single shared trust-safety µservice across 5 categories with 7 regulatory regimes is the load-bearing risk). Keeping at MAJOR.

findings.title: Build-ahead-of-certification creates EU AI Act + GDPR Article 25 legal exposure that the bundle does not weigh
findings.evidence_excerpt: ADR-0250 §purpose: build features ahead of certification, gate via Cedar fragment until certified per-region.
findings.ground_truth: EU AI Act Article 6 + Annex III define high-risk AI systems by their PURPOSE, not by their gate status. A high-risk AI system that exists in the codebase with a Cedar gate is 'placed on the market' for the purposes of the Act (per Meta Threads delayed-launch precedent in EU). GDPR Article 25 'data protection by design and by default' arguably requires PII-processing features to be certified BEFORE THE CODE EXISTS, not just before the gate opens. The bundle does not weigh these.
findings.why_this_matters: Build-ahead-of-certification optimizes for engineering velocity at the cost of legal exposure. A misconfigured Cedar fragment, leaked admin panel, or debug endpoint that bypasses Cedar turns built-but-gated into shipped-but-uncertified. The legal posture is more fragile than the engineering posture suggests.
findings.fix: AMEND ADR-0250 §Per-Class-Certification-Order: for EU AI Act high-risk classes, GDPR special-category PII, PCI-DSS scope, HIPAA scope — certification gates BUILD, not just the gate-flag. For lower-risk classes, build-ahead is permitted. The audience-tier matrix (ADR-0244) drives the per-class differentiation.
findings.self_audit: Could the author refute? Author could counter: 'build-ahead-of-certification with Cedar-gating IS the by-design protection per GDPR Article 25; the gate is the design control'. Partially valid; this is a legal-interpretation question that needs council-legal sign-off, not a unilateral engineering decision. Keeping at MAJOR with MEDIUM confidence (the legal interpretation is contested; the M1 lens flags it for explicit legal review).

findings.title: MLS RFC 9420 is younger than Signal Protocol in production deployment; bundle does not weigh the production-validation asymmetry
findings.evidence_excerpt: Deep-dive §4.5 reviews MLS RFC 9420 as canonical. The bundle does not contain an explicit MLS-vs-Signal comparison.
findings.ground_truth: MLS RFC 9420 ratified 2023; ~2 years production deployment at hyperscaler scale (Webex, Wire, Wickr). Signal Protocol: ~12 years production at WhatsApp + Signal + Skype + Google Messages. Production-validation asymmetry is ~10 years.
findings.why_this_matters: Production validation asymmetry is not by itself a reason to reject MLS — but the bundle's silence about the asymmetry is the M1 finding. Choosing MLS may be right; choosing MLS without weighing Signal Protocol's longer track record is asymmetric.
findings.fix: ADD keystone-bundle §E2E-Counter-Pattern: explicit comparison of MLS RFC 9420 vs Signal Protocol with reversal-cost-from-MLS-to-Signal at year N. If MLS still wins, the argument is visible. Cheap to add.
findings.self_audit: Could the author refute? Yes — MLS group-chat scalability is the differentiator, and Signal Protocol's group-chat is patent-encumbered. The argument is reasonable. Downgraded from MAJOR to MINOR because this is a contested-but-defensible choice; the M1 finding is about argument transparency, not about the choice itself.

findings.title: Bominal-inheritance treated as evidence-source equivalent to AWS/GCP/Azure; Bominal is a parallel codebase, not a production-at-scale validation
findings.evidence_excerpt: Five keystone ADRs (0242, 0243, 0245, 0246, 0248) cite feedback_bominal_inheritance_precedence in §related_memory.
findings.ground_truth: Per project memory `feedback_bominal_inheritance_precedence` and `feedback_flat_product_catalog`, Bominal is a parallel codebase (oyatie ≡ Bominal parallel codebase). Bominal is not documented as a production-at-scale validation at AWS/GCP/Azure scale. Treating Bominal precedent as evidence equivalent to hyperscaler production is asymmetric.
findings.why_this_matters: The bundle inherits multiple load-bearing premises (oyatie-is-a-tenant, Cedar-as-universal-gate, audience-as-tenant-property) from Bominal without independent oyatie-specific evidence. The Bominal-inheritance pattern silences the M1 lens for inherited premises.
findings.fix: ADD ADR-NNNN-bominal-inheritance-as-evidence: explicitly bound when Bominal precedent counts as evidence. For naming + glossary + structure: yes (low-stakes, high-reuse). For scale-sensitive architectural choices (tenancy topology, cellular shape, policy engine): only with independent oyatie-specific evidence. Annotate each Bominal-inherited doctrine in the bundle with its evidence tier.
findings.self_audit: Could the author refute? Author could counter: 'Bominal-inheritance is a NAMING + STRUCTURE convention, not a load-bearing architectural evidence source'. Counter-counter: the bundle's own §related_memory cites Bominal-inheritance alongside architectural-class memories (feedback_quality_performance_scalability_bar, feedback_clean_architecture_requirements). The author's distinction is not the bundle's. Keeping at MAJOR.

ambiguity_risks.quote: partial acceptance is rejected because the doctrines are mutually-reinforcing and produced together to avoid the drift pattern that produced ADR-0220 → ADR-0239 amendment within twelve days
ambiguity_risks.interpretation_a: Bundling 14 ADRs prevents drift because cross-doctrine interaction effects are caught at draft time
ambiguity_risks.interpretation_b: Bundling 14 ADRs concentrates reversal risk; any one wrong premise sinks the bundle; the cited evidence (ADR-0220 → ADR-0239) actually shows that AMENDMENT PAIRS drift, not that INDEPENDENT ADRs drift
ambiguity_risks.risk_if_wrong: If interpretation B is correct, the bundle inherits the drift pattern at 14x amplification, with no per-doctrine reversal path

ambiguity_risks.quote: Establish `oyatie` as the canonical, first-class, reserved-namespace org-tenant of its own multi-tenant platform
ambiguity_risks.interpretation_a: We run ourselves as a customer; operational uniformity wins; matches Bominal precedent
ambiguity_risks.interpretation_b: We run a privileged control-plane subsystem labeled 'tenant'; the label is marketing; the operational reality is control-plane-with-break-glass; matches AWS/GCP/Azure precedent
ambiguity_risks.risk_if_wrong: If interpretation B is the operational reality, the bundle's claim of 'no internal carve-outs, no bypass paths' is false at the bootstrap layer, and the doctrine fails its own coherence test

ambiguity_risks.quote: EVERY routing, authorization, activation, attribution, retention, eligibility, gate, and decision-with-policy-implication in the oyatie platform is evaluated by the Cedar policy engine
ambiguity_risks.interpretation_a: Cedar is the canonical decision engine; library-mode + per-cell evaluators + per-µservice fragment subsets prevent the universal-gateway smell
ambiguity_risks.interpretation_b: Cedar is the universal gateway for policy decisions; ADR-0145 retired the universal-gateway shape for API calls; ADR-0243 reintroduces it for policy calls; the shape is identical at a different layer
ambiguity_risks.risk_if_wrong: If interpretation B is correct, the platform's gating logic is bottlenecked by a single engine's continued investment by Amazon, with reversal cost 7-8

ambiguity_risks.quote: BYOK-everywhere as the canonical credential model: the substrate owns zero credentials
ambiguity_risks.interpretation_a: Every credential is owned by the caller; substrate has zero custody liability; works for all audiences
ambiguity_risks.interpretation_b: BYOK works for B2B audiences; for B2C consumer audiences, BYOK is hostile UX and requires a managed-key carve-out that the doctrine forbids; the doctrine cannot ship as-written for B2C
ambiguity_risks.risk_if_wrong: If interpretation B is correct, B2C consumer AI features fail at launch, or the doctrine carves out an exception that violates its own framing

multi_perspective_notes.executor: An executor implementing the bundle as-written must: (a) bootstrap the `oyatie` tenant before the tenancy µservice exists (recursion unaddressed); (b) implement Cedar gates for 16 distinct decision classes including feature flags + capability routing + data classification (each is a distinct domain); (c) dissolve foundry while the M02-P06 supervisor-language premise is unresolved; (d) deploy four-tier cells before there are tenants to put in them; (e) implement BYOK-everywhere knowing B2C UX fails. Each of these is an executor-visible defect that the bundle's all-or-nothing framing prevents the executor from raising.
multi_perspective_notes.stakeholder: A stakeholder reviewing the bundle is asked to accept 14 doctrines as one commitment. The framing pre-empts the M1 lens's most valuable verdict (accept-most-defer-some). The drift evidence cited (ADR-0220 → ADR-0239 12-day amendment) is interpreted by the bundle as 'staged acceptance fails, so we bundle'; the same evidence supports 'amendment pairs drift, so we improve up-front design' — which is what the bundle ALSO does. Bundling and up-front-design are orthogonal; conflating them is the meta-fallacy.
multi_perspective_notes.skeptic: The strongest argument against the bundle in its current form: NINE load-bearing premises (P1-P9 + the Bominal-inheritance meta-premise) are asserted with asymmetric evidence (only cited material supporting the chosen path; counter-patterns omitted). The bundle's all-or-nothing framing makes it the most expensive thing to reverse. Reversal cost compounds across premises. Any one wrong premise sinks the bundle. The probability that NONE of the 9 premises is wrong, given the evidence asymmetry and the 30-day churn cycle observed in ADR-0220 → ADR-0239 → ADR-0220-superseded-by-ADR-0255, is low. The strongest argument FOR the bundle (the defender's case): 'mutual reinforcement is real; per-ADR review missed the interaction effects; the bundle is the only way to catch them'. That defense survives some scrutiny BUT does not survive the M1 lens's specific question: 'why is mutual reinforcement incompatible with staged acceptance?' The answer the bundle gives — 'staged acceptance drifts' — is contradicted by the bundle's own willingness to use staged ENFORCEMENT (`advisory-until-X-lands` across every keystone). If staged ENFORCEMENT is acceptable, staged ACCEPTANCE is also acceptable. The framing is inconsistent.

verdict_justification: NO-GO-AS-BUNDLE is the M1 verdict. The bundle's all-or-nothing framing is the primary failure mode (M1-KB-F1 CRITICAL). Two additional CRITICAL findings (M1-KB-F2 oyatie-is-a-tenant evidence gap, plus the failure of the bundle to consider its own M1-most-valuable alternative verdict) and six MAJOR findings (M1-KB-F3 through M1-KB-F8 plus M1-KB-F10) compound to a bundle that locks 9 load-bearing premises with asymmetric evidence at compounded reversibility cost. The bundle's own enforcement_status pattern (`advisory-until-X-lands`) admits that staged enforcement is acceptable; the framing's refusal of staged acceptance is internally inconsistent. Alternative paths exist: (a) 3-wave split per ALT-9 with independent multispectrum review per wave; (b) GO-WITH-EXPLICIT-REVERSAL-CLAUSES where every ADR adds §Pre-Committed-Escape-Hatch; (c) DEFER 6 OF 14 (0247, 0249, 0250, 0252, 0254, 0255) pending evidence threshold. The review STARTED in ADVERSARIAL mode and STAYED there because each premise audited surfaced at least one CRITICAL or MAJOR gap. No CRITICAL or MAJOR finding downgrades on Realist Check. The bundle should not ship as 14-of-14 with partial-acceptance-rejected gating. If the bundle authors return with: (a) explicit M1-challenge sections per ADR addressing the 10 challenged-assumptions above; OR (b) a 3-wave split with independent review per wave; OR (c) a 6-of-14 defer plan; the verdict upgrades to REVISE. Without one of those, the bundle is locking-in 9 load-bearing premises with asymmetric evidence at compounded reversibility cost.

principle_option_consistency.reason: Bundle's stated principle (mutual reinforcement requires bundled acceptance) is inconsistent with its own use of staged enforcement (advisory-until-X-lands). Staged enforcement IS staged acceptance with a different label.

alternatives_depth.reason: 9 alternative paths exist (ALT-1 through ALT-9, enumerated above). None of the 9 is considered in the bundle. Comparison set is artificially narrow across multiple ADRs.

risk_verification_rigor.reason: Per-ADR risks are enumerated; cross-ADR interaction risks are surfaced in the deep-dive (§3 anti-pattern smells, §4 migration-pain scoring). But the META-RISK ('what if the bundling framing is itself wrong?') is not in any risk table. Missing meta-risk: the bundle's own framing.

deliberate_additions.reason: Pre-mortem in deep-dive §3 enumerates anti-pattern smells but does not include 'bundle fails because partial-acceptance-rejected concentrates reversal risk'. Pre-mortem is technically sound but framing-blind.

open_questions: Why is the 'partial acceptance rejected' framing not subject to its own M1 challenge inside the bundle?
Does the bundle authors' bar for 'mutually reinforcing' actually mean 'inseparable' or does it mean 'reviewed together'?
What is the explicit reversal cost (in engineering-months) for each of the 9 load-bearing premises if it turns out wrong?
Has the AWS/GCP/Azure control-plane separation pattern been considered as an alternative to oyatie-is-a-tenant?
Has OPA + Rego been considered as an alternative to Cedar?
Has Stripe-style regional active-active with shard groups been considered as an alternative to Amazon-shape four-tier cells?
What is the documented N threshold at which the Amazon-shape cellular pattern's overhead is justified?
What is the credential model for B2C consumer AI features under BYOK-everywhere?

Has the prior M02-P06 M1 review's open questions (Siigari/claude-heartbeat adopt-vs-reimplement; supervisor language ADR; N threshold for drift detection) been resolved before propagating Foundry dissolution into Workflow Engine + Intelligence?
Has the EU AI Act 'placed on the market' interpretation been reviewed by council-legal for the build-ahead-of-certification doctrine?
What is the fallback path if the unified multi-category marketplace doctrine proves unworkable in production?
When does Bominal precedent count as evidence, and when does it not?
